report.how_it_happened: The gateway router had no per-ticket-type routes, so every ticket used the default model. CHG-5120 (Sep 8, 25% to Osric 2 Thinking), CHG-5124 (Sep 9, 60%), and CHG-5129 (Sep 10, 100%) rolled Osric to all tickets. Daily spend stepped from ~$5.2k to ~$7.6k on weekdays starting Sep 8–10. Osric 2 Thinking generates far more output units per ticket (e.g., 32,300 reasoning units for Technical troubleshooting vs 300 for Vesk 4) at a higher output price, so cost per ticket rose from $0.0430 to $0.0542 even as ticket volume was flat and unit prices fell.
report.quality_impact: Resolution rate fell from 84.5% to 83.0%. Osric 2 Thinking is below the quality bar (Vesk 4 minus 2 points) for Technical troubleshooting (72% vs 74% bar) and Integrations & API (64% vs 69% bar), so the setup running today does not meet the quality bar for those two types. The proposed setup meets the bar for every type: Vesk 4 Lite (92.1% vs 91% bar for Account & password; 88.2% vs 87% bar for Billing) and Vesk 4 (76% vs 74% for Technical troubleshooting; 71% vs 69% for Integrations & API).

attribution.explanation: The Osric 2 Thinking rollout (CHG-5120/5124/5129) made Osric the default model for all ticket types. Per the eval report, Osric uses vastly more output units per ticket than Vesk 4 (e.g., 32,300 vs 300 reasoning units for Technical troubleshooting), and per the price schedule Osric's output price is $1.90 per 1M units. The combination of much higher unit volume and the rollout to 100% of tickets drove daily spend from ~$5.2k to ~$7.6k on weekdays, raising cost per ticket from $0.0430 to $0.0542. The earlier changes (CHG-5031 on Aug 19 and CHG-5107 on Sep 3) did not coincide with any metric move.

report.manager_summary: Your AI help-desk bill rose about 30% this month (Sep 1–21 vs Aug 1–21), from $94.4k to $122.7k. Ticket volume only grew about 3%, while the unit price fell by half. The real cause is a sharp jump in units used per ticket, which began when the team switched the default model to Osric 2 Thinking between Sep 8 and Sep 10. That model uses far more output units per ticket, especially for technical and integration questions, and quality slipped: resolution fell from 84.5% to 83.0%. I prepared a routing change (pending your approval) that sends simpler tickets to a cheaper model and keeps a stronger model for the harder ones. It is projected to cut cost per ticket from $0.0542 to about $0.0290, saving roughly $102.6k per month, while meeting the quality bar for every ticket type.
